mechanism: EXG202 is an investigational recombinant AAV gene therapy for neovascular/wet AMD delivered by a single intravitreal injection. ClinicalTrials.gov describes EXG202 as intended to provide durable expression of therapeutic intraocular protein. Exegenesis/Jiayin's HKEX application proof describes EXG202 as using the proprietary EOC024 capsid, engineered through the AAVarta AI-aided platform to traverse the inner limiting membrane and broaden retinal transduction, with a transgene product designed to inhibit key angiogenic pathways.
phase: Early Phase 1 for assigned IIT record NCT06888492; separate EXG202-111 record NCT07178249 is Phase 1/2.
development_status: NCT06888492 is a not-yet-recruiting, open-label, non-randomized, sequential dose-escalation Early Phase 1 study in China evaluating two intravitreal EXG202 dose cohorts in 8 participants with wet/neovascular AMD; estimated start is 2025-03-28, estimated primary completion is 2026-04-25, estimated study completion is 2026-04-30, and no results are posted. A separate EXG202 Phase 1/2 study, NCT07178249, is also not yet recruiting, plans 60 participants, has estimated start 2025-10-16, estimated primary completion 2028-02-28, and estimated study completion 2032-12-30. Exegenesis/Jiayin's HKEX application proof states EXG202 received FDA IND clearance in July 2025 and NMPA IND approval in August 2025, and that an IIT was being conducted for early safety, tolerability, and biological-activity insights.
expected_launch_window: 2033 or later unless Phase 1/2 data support an accelerated or otherwise shortened regulatory path
clinical_summary: EXG202 could be clinically differentiated if it delivers durable anti-angiogenic control after one office-based intravitreal injection, because current branded anti-VEGF therapy for wet AMD still requires repeated intravitreal injections. The company positions EXG202 as a next-generation intravitreal AAV approach with broader retinal transduction and multi-pathway angiogenic inhibition, and the later Phase 1/2 protocol explicitly describes EXG202 as an rAAV vector carrying a coding sequence for a soluble anti-VEGF protein. Current evidence remains early: both direct EXG202 CT.gov records are not yet recruiting and have no posted results, while company statements on safety and preliminary efficacy are not yet supported by public, peer-reviewed EXG202 clinical data.
safety_summary: NCT06888492's primary endpoint is the frequency, type, and intensity of ocular and non-ocular adverse events and serious adverse events through Week 52, including exploration of maximum tolerated dose. NCT07178249 also focuses on AEs, SAEs, and dose-limiting toxicity through Week 52. Key launch safety issues to monitor include ocular inflammation, endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, retinal vasculitis or occlusion, intraocular pressure increase, immune response to AAV capsid or transgene product, need for steroid prophylaxis, and rescue anti-VEGF use. Current anti-VEGF analog labels and policies establish baseline intravitreal-injection monitoring expectations, but EXG202-specific clinical safety data are not posted.
management_tools: Track NCT06888492 and NCT07178249 recruiting status, dose escalation updates, posted results, conference presentations, and any FDA/NMPA protocol progression.
Medical-benefit prior authorization for any future launch, requiring labeled diagnosis of wet/neovascular AMD and retinal specialist prescribing/administration.
Require baseline OCT, BCVA, disease activity, prior anti-VEGF response, lesion laterality, and absence of ocular/periocular infection or active intraocular inflammation.
Use quantity limits tied to final label, likely one EXG202 administration per treated eye unless retreatment is supported.
Require documentation of peri-procedural steroid or inflammation-monitoring protocol if included in final trial regimen or label.

Define continuation and outcomes monitoring around BCVA, OCT fluid/anatomy, central retinal thickness, rescue anti-VEGF injections, ocular inflammation, IOP changes, retinal vasculitis/occlusion, and serious ocular events.
Avoid duplicate payment for chronic anti-VEGF therapy in the same eye after EXG202 except for documented rescue or label-supported combination use.
Prepare first-year medical-benefit scenarios for one-time ophthalmic gene therapy pricing, bilateral treatment rules, outcomes-based agreements, installment payment, and site-of-care controls.
evidence_gaps: No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted for NCT06888492 or NCT07178249.
Both direct EXG202 CT.gov records were listed as not yet recruiting in the structured CT.gov data checked for this packet.
No peer-reviewed EXG202 human efficacy or safety publication was found.
The HKEX application proof reports excellent safety and preliminary efficacy, but detailed EXG202 clinical data were not found in public registry results or publications.
Final therapeutic protein sequence, dose, steroid prophylaxis, retreatment rules, bilateral treatment approach, and rescue anti-VEGF algorithm remain unclear.
No public EXG202 price, WAC, net-cost estimate, or contracting approach exists; annual cost is analog-derived.

sources.title: To Evaluate the Safety and Preliminary Efficacy of Intravitreal EXG202 Injection in Patients with Wet (neovascular) Age-related Macular Degeneration (wAMD)
supports: Assigned EXG202 trial record; sponsor is Guangzhou Jiayin Biotech Ltd and other study ID is EXG202-011.
Open-label, non-randomized, sequential dose-escalation Early Phase 1 study in wet/neovascular AMD.
Overall status is not yet recruiting; estimated enrollment is 8; estimated start is 2025-03-28; estimated primary completion is 2026-04-25; estimated study completion is 2026-04-30.
Intervention is Biological: EXG202, described as a gene therapy product for wet AMD with single intravitreal injection and administration.
Primary outcome is safety and tolerability through Week 52, including ocular and non-ocular AEs/SAEs and maximum tolerated dose exploration.
Secondary outcomes include BCVA change from baseline and OCT through 52 weeks.
Eligibility requires wet AMD with active lesions, ETDRS BCVA 73-19 letters, and clinically meaningful response to standard anti-VEGF therapy within 6 months before screening or during lead-in.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: Evaluating the Safety and Preliminary Efficacy of EXG202 Gene Therapy for Neovascular AMD
supports: Separate direct EXG202 clinical trial record; sponsor is Guangzhou Jiayin Biotech Ltd and other study ID is EXG202-111.
Phase 1/2, open-label, non-randomized, sequential study in wet/neovascular AMD with four intravitreal EXG202 dose-escalation cohorts.
Overall status is not yet recruiting; estimated enrollment is 60; estimated start is 2025-10-16; estimated primary completion is 2028-02-28; estimated study completion is 2032-12-30.
Brief summary describes EXG202 as a recombinant AAV gene therapy vector carrying a coding sequence for a soluble anti-VEGF protein after one-time treatment.
Primary outcomes include Week 52 AEs/SAEs/dose-limiting toxicity and BCVA change from baseline; a secondary safety endpoint assesses AEs/SAEs through Week 24.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false.

sources.title: Application Proof of Exegenesis Bio Inc.
supports: Exegenesis Bio application proof describes EXG202 as a key product for fundus neovascularization diseases including wAMD, DME, and RVO.

EXG202 is described as using the proprietary EOC024 capsid engineered through the AAVarta AI-driven evolution platform to traverse the inner limiting membrane and achieve deeper and broader retinal transduction.
Nonhuman primate studies reportedly showed approximately 2- to 5-fold higher therapeutic protein expression in retinal tissues compared with benchmark intravitreal AAV capsid AAV2.7m8.
The company states the expressed transgene product enables coordinated inhibition of key angiogenic pathways.
Application proof states EXG202 received FDA IND approval/clearance in July 2025 and NMPA IND approval in August 2025.

Application proof states the company was conducting an EXG202 investigator-initiated trial to obtain early safety, tolerability, and biological-activity insights after intravitreal administration in wAMD patients.
Commercial strategy positions EXG202 as a durable, single-injection intravitreal gene therapy intended to reduce dosing and surgical burden.

sources.title: AAV-based gene therapies for neovascular AMD
supports: Review states nAMD is driven by choroidal neovascularization and dysregulated VEGF signaling.
Current nAMD standard therapy involves repeated intravitreal anti-VEGF injections, often monthly or bimonthly, creating treatment burden.
AAV-based gene therapy offers sustained intraocular delivery of anti-angiogenic agents with a single treatment and could reduce frequent injection needs.
Review highlights challenges for AAV-based nAMD gene therapy, including preexisting neutralizing antibodies and inflammation.

sources.title: DailyMed: VABYSMO (faricimab-svoa) injection
supports: Vabysmo is indicated for neovascular/wet AMD.

Recommended nAMD dosing is four initial monthly intravitreal injections followed by OCT and visual-acuity assessments to determine Q16W, Q12W, or Q8W maintenance dosing; some patients may need monthly dosing after the first four doses.
Vabysmo is a VEGF and Ang-2 inhibitor, providing an approved multi-pathway anti-angiogenic analog for wet AMD.
Label identifies contraindications including ocular/periocular infection, active intraocular inflammation, and hypersensitivity.

sources.title: DailyMed: EYLEA HD (aflibercept) injection
supports: Eylea HD is indicated for neovascular/wet AMD.

Recommended wet AMD dosing includes three initial monthly intravitreal injections followed by dosing every 8 to 16 weeks, with possible monthly dosing for some patients and extended every-20-week dosing after one year of successful response.
Label warnings include endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, retinal vasculitis with or without occlusion, increased intraocular pressure, and arterial thromboembolic events.
Analog label supports monitoring expectations for intravitreal retinal therapies.

sources.title: EYLEA HD Connecticut Drug Cost Education
supports: Regeneron lists EYLEA HD 8 mg/0.07 mL vial WAC as $2,812.98.
WAC is defined as the manufacturer's undiscounted list price to wholesalers as reported to third-party drug pricing publishers.
WAC does not represent actual transaction price and excludes discounts, rebates, and other reductions.

sources.title: Cigna: LUXTURNA - First gene therapy to treat a rare form of inherited vision loss
supports: Luxturna is an FDA-approved ocular gene therapy manufactured by Spark Therapeutics.
Cigna reported Luxturna WAC of $425,000 per eye or $850,000 for both eyes.
Luxturna is covered under medical benefit plans subject to medical necessity review.
Cigna described one course of therapy as one injection per eye and noted additional facility and professional administration charges.

sources.title: Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 0701: Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Inhibitors for Ocular Indications
supports: Aetna lists precertification contact instructions for multiple ocular VEGF inhibitors including Eylea, Eylea HD, Vabysmo, Lucentis, and Susvimo.
Aetna considers aflibercept and faricimab medically necessary for neovascular/wet AMD when criteria are met.
Continuation of aflibercept or faricimab requires positive clinical response such as improvement or maintenance in BCVA or visual field, or reduction in vision decline or severe vision-loss risk.
Susvimo criteria require wet AMD diagnosis, prior response to at least two intravitreal VEGF inhibitor injections within the past 6 months, and use with the ocular implant.

expected_launch_window.value: 2033 or later unless Phase 1/2 data support an accelerated or otherwise shortened regulatory path
expected_launch_window.method: Used direct EXG202 registry status, Phase 1/2 primary completion in 2028, study completion in 2032, lack of posted results, and absence of any public Phase 3, BLA/NDA, approval, or launch guidance.
expected_launch_window.explanation: A near-term launch is not source-supported. EXG202 has IND clearance and early clinical activity, but current public records support a long development path with Phase 1/2 follow-up extending to 2032 before any standard late-stage filing pathway.

annual_cost_range.method: Low estimate uses current branded wet AMD anti-VEGF analog Eylea HD WAC of $2,812.98 multiplied by five first-year labeled doses under the three-loading-dose plus Q16W maintenance scenario. High estimate uses one-time ocular gene therapy Luxturna WAC of $425,000 per treated eye.
annual_cost_range.explanation: EXG202 has no disclosed price. The low end anchors to a durable branded wet AMD anti-VEGF regimen; the high end anchors to an approved one-time ocular gene therapy. The range excludes rebates, bilateral treatment, facility/professional fees, imaging, steroid prophylaxis, adverse-event management, and rescue anti-VEGF injections.

clinical_differentiation.method: Balanced one-time intravitreal AAV delivery, company-described broader retinal transduction, and multi-pathway anti-angiogenic design against very early clinical stage and lack of posted EXG202 results.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: If confirmed, EXG202 could materially reduce treatment burden versus repeated anti-VEGF injections and avoid subretinal surgery. The rating is not high because public efficacy and safety evidence remains preliminary and mostly company-disclosed.

budget_impact.method: Assessed prevalent wet AMD population, medical-benefit administration, possible one-time gene therapy pricing, bilateral-disease potential, and analog anti-VEGF payer controls.
budget_impact.explanation: Even with uncertain launch timing, a durable intravitreal gene therapy for a high-prevalence retinal disease could create high first-year exposure if priced closer to ocular gene therapy analogs and used broadly.

disruption_risk.method: Rated from early Phase 1/2 status and long follow-up horizon, offset by potentially disruptive one-time intravitreal gene therapy design for a repeated-injection standard-of-care market.
disruption_risk.explanation: Operational disruption is not imminent, but positive data could change wet AMD treatment pathways, anti-VEGF utilization, rescue-injection protocols, and medical-benefit contracting.

recommended_action.method: Matched action to not-yet-recruiting CT.gov status, lack of posted clinical results, no Phase 3 or filing guidance, and high but distant potential budget impact.
recommended_action.explanation: Monitor registry updates, first human data, dose selection, and regulatory progression before drafting final coverage criteria; maintain early scenario notes for one-time intravitreal gene therapy pricing and rescue anti-VEGF management.

quality_flags: Both direct EXG202 CT.gov records checked for this packet list overall status as not yet recruiting and have no posted results.
The assigned NCT06888492 record is Early Phase 1 with only 8 estimated participants; the broader EXG202-111 Phase 1/2 record NCT07178249 should be tracked alongside it.
Company HKEX application proof reports IND approvals and preliminary clinical safety/efficacy, but detailed EXG202 patient-level or peer-reviewed data were not found.

EXG202 appears connected to Exegenesis Bio/Jiayin based on CT.gov sponsor name, Exegenesis email contact, and HKEX application proof; the assigned manufacturer name was retained as Guangzhou Jiayin Biotech Ltd.

Annual cost is analog-derived because no EXG202 price exists; low end uses first-year Eylea HD WAC under an extended labeled wet AMD dosing scenario and high end uses Luxturna ocular gene therapy WAC per eye.

Cost range is per first treated eye for planning; bilateral treatment, administration, imaging, steroid prophylaxis, adverse-event care, rescue anti-VEGF therapy, rebates, and outcomes-based contracts could materially change budget impact.
